- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish, model lags in correction; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; use 10–15% smoothing on forecast curve.
